newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium to rebound to $1,700/50 next year - Man.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium to rebound to $1,700/50 next year - Man.

text.p: The aluminium market, depressed by weak sentiment, speculative selling and stock increases, should bottom out over the next one or two months, E D & F Man said.

Prices are expected to slide to lows around $1,275 to $1,325 per tonne before the end of this year but seasonal buying and slightly tighter supply should begin to set the scene for next year's recovery, it said in a report by Frederick Demler.
Economic growth next year is seen leading to firmer demand while production should slow, sparking a rebound to $1,700/50. As destocking ends, prices should end 1997 at an average of $1,525, it added.

The stocks/consumption ratio, currently at 9.6 weeks, is expected to decline to 8.6 weeks in the fourth quarter, to 7.6 weeks in the second quarter 1997 and edge back up to 7.8 weeks by the fourth quarter 1997.
Despite the negative sentiment engulfing prices, the market has seen some positive shifts recently.
Shipments have rebounded after hitting a low in January this year and production growth has slowed.
Limited production restarts are seen this year and in 1997 with only moderate capacity builds expected over the next two years, Man said.
Net East Bloc sales are topping out and the stock declines as traced by the International Primary Aluminium Institute are offsetting the builds in London Metal Exchange inventories.
